subject: Nimbus Payments — retention & deletion evidence (SOC 2 / ISO request)
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@nimbus-pay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus Payments Security <security@nimbus-pay.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retention & deletion evidence request (SOC 2 / ISO)

Hi Rafael,

As part of our vendor risk review for Redwood we need evidence demonstrating your retention and deletion controls for customer data and logs. Specifically Nimbus is focused on: 

- Data residency assurances for production artifacts and backups (where data-at-rest is stored geographically)
- Retention windows applied to primary stores and backups (policies + proof of enforcement)
- Deletion workflows and runbook evidence (how deletions are executed and audited)
- Any residual in-memory/KV cache or model context persistence and how/when it is erased

Could you provide:
1) Current retention policy document or excerpt that covers logs, user content, embeddings, and backups
2) A sample job log or audit entry proving deletion ran for a sample record (can be redacted)
3) The S3 lifecycle/export of rules that show auto-delete/transition timing
4) Clarification on backups: immutable snapshots vs lifecycle deletes and retention length

We are working toward a tight deadline for our internal SOC 2 control mapping next week. If you can get the above by Tuesday 23 Jun that would be ideal — otherwise let us know a target date.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Desai
Senior InfoSec Manager, Nimbus Payments
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@nimbus-pay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention & deletion evidence request (SOC 2 / ISO)

Priya — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (legal/compliance) and Ben (security eng) to assemble the artifacts and provide technical details. Quick summary and what we'll attach now: 

What you'll get in this thread (attached):
- redwood-data-retention-policy-v2.pdf — policy covering logs, user content, embeddings, backups, and backups-of-backups
- s3-lifecycle-rules-export-20260620.csv — exported lifecycle rules for the buckets that contain production artifacts
- data-erasure-runbook.md — actionable runbook describing deletion job steps and approvals
- deletion-job-logs-20260620.zip — redacted job logs showing a deletion cycle for a sample tenant (timestamps and job IDs included)

Short answers to your numbered questions:
1) Policy: retention windows are explicit per class (logs: 90 days; embeddings: 365 days default; user content: customer-configurable, default 365 days; backups: 30 days snapshot retention + 365 days cold backup)
2) Proof: see deletion-job-logs (redactions applied) and the runbook that maps audit IDs to jobs
3) S3 lifecycle: attached CSV shows transition to GLACIER/COLD storage and expiration rules; we include bucket ARNs in the Drive link
4) Backups: we use snapshot-based backups stored in region-specific buckets; snapshots are immutable while retained, and expiration is controlled by the lifecycle job; backups older than retention are permanently deleted by background jobs and logged to audit.

We'll follow up with an answer on KV cache and model-context persistence (that requires Ben to confirm exact eviction and scrub cycles).

Next steps: Ben/Neha — can you confirm the KV cache scrubbing cadence and any additional audit markers to include? Priya — want these files uploaded to your secure share or is email ok for the redacted artifacts?

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@nimbus-pay.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retention & deletion evidence request (SOC 2 / ISO)

Thanks Rafael — quick technical note on caches and model context: 

- KV cache / in-memory caches: ephemeral across serving instances; we employ strict TTLs and LRU eviction. For our hosted offering, cache shards are destroyed on instance termination and a final scrub routine zeroes memory pages where supported by the OS/hypervisor.
- Long-term context: we do NOT persist user-level prompt context or conversation context to long-term storage unless the customer opts in to conversation history. Default behavior: context exists only in transit and in RAM/ephemeral storage during inference.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: embeddings stored in the embedding-store are subject to the retention policy (default 365 days) and deletions are implemented by background jobs that produce audit entries.

Evidence we can provide in addition to the attachments:
- cache-scrub-excerpt-20260622.txt (example run output)
- audit-index-map-20260620.csv (redacted map of audit IDs to deletion jobs)

If Nimbus needs exact OS-level memory dump proofs we can coordinate with Neha/legal and your security contact but typically the combination of runbook + job logs + cache scrub excerpts satisfy SOC 2 auditors.

Ben Carter
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Rafael / Neha / Ben — received all artifacts and the Drive link. Reviewing now. Two quick clarifications before we close the control: 

1) Are deletion audit IDs bound to customer tenant IDs in the audit-index-map? We need to map deletion activity back to tenant boundaries for our control evidence.
2) For backups: confirm whether cold backups are region-replicated (cross-region) by default or retained only in-region; also need the maximum retention in days for backups-of-backups.

If you can respond to those two points today we'll close this item on our side. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Priya
